items.title: The Life of the Buddha and the Four Sights
items.description: Animated and documentary clips covering Siddhartha Gautama's early life, the Four Sights and his journey to Enlightenment under the Bodhi tree.

items.title: Dependent Origination and the Wheel of Life
items.description: Visual explanations of conditionality, the 12 links (nidanas) and how the Tibetan Wheel of Life illustrates the cycle of samsara.

items.title: Three Marks of Existence: Dukkha, Anicca and Anatta
items.description: Short revision videos unpacking each of the Three Marks of Existence and their significance for Buddhist understanding of the world.

items.title: Seneca: Buddhism Beliefs
items.description: Bitesize revision pages covering the Buddha's life, the Dhamma and the Three Marks of Existence with key vocabulary and activities.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: Buddhism
items.description: In-depth background articles on Buddhist beliefs, history and the significance of Nibbana — useful for extending your understanding.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Adaptive recall quizzes on Buddhism beliefs including dependent origination, the Three Marks and the Dhamma.

items.title: The Buddha (Documentary)
items.description: A feature-length documentary tracing the life of Siddhartha Gautama from his sheltered princely upbringing through to his Enlightenment and the spread of the Dhamma.

items.title: The First Noble Truth: Dukkha Explained
items.description: Revision videos breaking down the three types of dukkha — painful experiences, change and all-pervasive suffering — with exam-style examples.

items.title: The Second Noble Truth: Tanha and the Three Poisons
items.description: Concise explanations of craving (tanha) and how the three poisons — attachment, aversion and ignorance — drive the cycle of suffering.

items.title: The Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta: The First Sermon
items.description: Clips and commentary on the Buddha's first teaching at Deer Park, Sarnath, which sets out the Four Noble Truths for the first time.

items.title: Seneca: The Four Noble Truths
items.description: Structured revision notes on dukkha and its causes, with key-term definitions and practice questions.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: The Four Noble Truths
items.description: Background reading on the nature of suffering in Buddhism, the concept of samudaya and the role of the three fires.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Interactive flashcard and quiz activities on the First and Second Noble Truths, tanha and the three poisons.

items.title: Buddhism: Suffering and the Path to Liberation
items.description: Documentary exploring how Buddhists understand and respond to suffering in daily life, from monastery to modern city.

items.title: The Third Noble Truth: Nibbana and the Cessation of Suffering
items.description: Revision clips explaining what nibbana means, different interpretations of Enlightenment and its relationship to the end of the rebirth cycle.

items.title: The Eightfold Path Explained
items.description: Step-by-step videos covering all eight elements of the Eightfold Path and how they group into the Threefold Way of sila, samadhi and panna.

items.title: The Threefold Way: Ethics, Meditation and Wisdom
items.description: Clear explanations of how the three divisions of the Eightfold Path work together as a practical guide to Buddhist living.

items.title: Seneca: The Eightfold Path
items.description: Revision notes on the Fourth Noble Truth, the Eightfold Path and the Threefold Way, with recall activities.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: The Eightfold Path
items.description: Background articles on what the path to Enlightenment involves in practice and how different Buddhist traditions interpret nibbana.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Adaptive quizzes covering nibbana, the Eightfold Path elements and the groupings of sila, samadhi and panna.

items.title: Mindfulness and the Path to Enlightenment
items.description: A documentary tracing how the Eightfold Path shapes Buddhist monastic and lay practice in the modern world.

items.title: The Five Khandas and Buddhist Human Personality
items.description: Revision videos on the five aggregates (khandas), how they relate to anatta and why there is no permanent fixed self in Buddhist thought.

items.title: Bodhisattva Ideal and Mahayana Buddhism
items.description: Accessible explanations of the Bodhisattva path, sunyata, buddha-nature and how the Mahayana tradition differs from Theravada.

items.title: Kamma, Metta and the Five Precepts
items.description: Videos covering Buddhist ethical principles — kamma, compassion (karuna), loving kindness (metta) and the Five Precepts — and how they guide moral action.

items.title: Seneca: Buddhist Ethics and Human Destiny
items.description: Revision notes on kamma, the Five Precepts, karuna and the Bodhisattva ideal with exam-style questions.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: Mahayana and Theravada Buddhism
items.description: Background articles on the main Buddhist traditions, the Bodhisattva concept, Pure Land Buddhism and the Heart Sutra.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Interactive recall activities on the five khandas, kamma, metta, the Five Precepts and divergences between Theravada and Mahayana.

items.title: Compassion in Action: Buddhist Ethics Today
items.description: A documentary exploring how metta, karuna and the Five Precepts shape the lives of Buddhist communities around the world.

items.title: Buddhist Puja, Chanting and Devotional Worship
items.description: Videos showing puja rituals, the use of malas and mantra in Buddhist worship, with explanations of their purpose and symbolism.

items.title: Types of Buddhist Meditation: Samatha, Vipassana and Mindfulness
items.description: Comparative overviews of the main forms of Buddhist meditation — Samatha, Vipassana, Zazen, metta bhavana and visualisation — and their role in the Eightfold Path.

items.title: Sacred Places: Bodh Gaya, Sarnath and Buddhist Pilgrimage
items.description: Documentaries and clips exploring Buddhist temples, gompas, viharas and the significance of key pilgrimage sites like Bodh Gaya and the Deer Park at Sarnath.

items.title: Seneca: Buddhist Worship and Sacred Places
items.description: Revision pages on Buddhist forms of worship, types of meditation and the importance of pilgrimage sites.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: Buddhist Worship and Rituals
items.description: Background reading on puja, chanting, the significance of mudras and the role of temples and shrines in Buddhist practice.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Recall quizzes on Buddhist worship, the forms of meditation, sacred places and the significance of artefacts and offerings.

items.title: Sacred Wonders: Buddhist Temples and Monasteries
items.description: BBC series exploring iconic religious sites, including Buddhist temples and monasteries, with stunning footage of worship and pilgrimage.

items.title: Extreme Pilgrim: Buddhism
items.description: A presenter immerses himself in Buddhist monastic life, exploring meditation practice and the meaning of sacred spaces first-hand.

items.title: The Sangha and the Three Jewels
items.description: Explainer videos on the role of the monastic and lay sangha, the Three Jewels and the ordination of monks and nuns.

items.title: Wesak and Buddhist Festivals
items.description: Videos covering the origins and customs of key Buddhist festivals including Wesak, Hanamatsuri, Vassa and Parinirvana Day across Theravada, Mahayana and Tibetan traditions.

items.title: Life as a Buddhist Monk: The Ten Precepts and Monastery Rules
items.description: Documentary-style clips showing monastic life, the Ten Precepts observed by monks and nuns and the role of Uposatha days.

items.title: Seneca: The Sangha and Buddhist Festivals
items.description: Revision notes on the Three Jewels, the role of the Sangha and the significance of major Buddhist festivals.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: Buddhist Festivals and the Sangha
items.description: Background articles on Wesak, Vassa and the importance of community in Buddhist practice across different traditions.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Adaptive quizzes on the Sangha, the Three Jewels, the Ten Precepts and the origins of key Buddhist festivals.

items.title: The Monastery: A Buddhist Community
items.description: A documentary following life inside a Buddhist monastery, exploring how the Sangha supports spiritual practice, observes festivals and maintains monastic discipline.

items.title: Buddhist Death Rituals: Theravada, Tibetan and Japanese Traditions
items.description: Comparative videos on how death and mourning are approached across Buddhist traditions, from Theravada funerals to the Japanese Obon festival and Tibetan practices.

items.title: The Tibetan Book of the Dead and Bardo
items.description: Explanations of the Bardo — the transition period between death and rebirth — and how the Tibetan Book of the Dead guides the deceased through it.

items.title: Obon: Japan's Buddhist Festival of the Dead
items.description: Videos exploring the Obon festival in Japan — its Buddhist origins, rituals for honouring ancestors and its cultural significance.

items.title: Seneca: Buddhist Attitudes to Death
items.description: Revision notes on Buddhist beliefs about death, rebirth and the six realms of existence, with exam-focused activities.

items.title: BBC Bitesize: Buddhism and Death
items.description: Background articles on Buddhist death customs, the Tibetan Book of the Dead, kamma and how impermanence shapes Buddhist mourning practices.

items.title: Seneca Learning: GCSE Religious Studies
items.description: Recall quizzes on Buddhist death rites, the significance of Bardo, Obon and the six realms of existence.

items.title: Life After Death: Buddhist Perspectives
items.description: A documentary examining what Buddhists believe happens after death, covering kamma, rebirth, the six realms and the role of death rituals across cultures.
